name: Commonly confused English words dataset
description: Pairs and triples of English words that learners confuse (affect/effect, lend/borrow, say/tell…), one row per word, with part of speech, meaning, an example and a memory tip.

data.meaning: to agree to take or receive something
data.tip: Accept starts with "ac" like "acquire" (you take something). Except starts with "ex" like "exclude" (you leave something out).

data.meaning: not including
data.tip: Accept starts with "ac" like "acquire" (you take something). Except starts with "ex" like "exclude" (you leave something out).

data.meaning: in fact, really
data.example: Actually, I'm from Canada, not the US.
data.tip: Actually means "in fact". Currently means "now". (In Spanish, French and other languages, a similar word means "now", which is why learners mix them up.)

data.meaning: now, at the present time
data.tip: Actually means "in fact". Currently means "now". (In Spanish, French and other languages, a similar word means "now", which is why learners mix them up.)

data.meaning: an opinion about what someone should do
data.example: Can I give you some advice?
data.tip: Advice (with c) is the noun, like "ice". Advise (with s) is the verb, and the s sounds like z.

data.meaning: to tell someone what you think they should do
data.example: I advise you to see a doctor.
data.tip: Advice (with c) is the noun, like "ice". Advise (with s) is the verb, and the s sounds like z.

data.meaning: to change or influence something
data.example: The cold weather affects my knees.
data.tip: Affect is the Action (a verb); Effect is the End result (a noun). If you can put "the" or "an" before it, you need effect.

data.meaning: a result or change caused by something
data.tip: Affect is the Action (a verb); Effect is the End result (a noun). If you can put "the" or "an" before it, you need effect.

data.meaning: without other people
data.tip: Alone is a fact (no one is with you). Lonely is a feeling (you are sad about it). You can be alone and happy.

data.meaning: unhappy because you are alone
data.example: He felt lonely in the new city.
data.tip: Alone is a fact (no one is with you). Lonely is a feeling (you are sad about it). You can be alone and happy.

data.meaning: before now, or sooner than expected
data.tip: Already = it happened (maybe early). Yet = we're waiting for it (questions and negatives, at the end). Still = it continues.

data.meaning: until now (in questions and negatives)
data.tip: Already = it happened (maybe early). Yet = we're waiting for it (questions and negatives, at the end). Still = it continues.

data.meaning: continuing, not finished
data.tip: Already = it happened (maybe early). Yet = we're waiting for it (questions and negatives, at the end). Still = it continues.

data.meaning: to help someone
data.tip: Attend = be present at (attend a class). Assist = help. (Learners who speak Spanish or French often say "assist a class" by mistake.)

data.meaning: to go to an event or place
data.tip: Attend = be present at (attend a class). Assist = help. (Learners who speak Spanish or French often say "assist a class" by mistake.)

data.meaning: next to, at the side of
data.tip: Beside = by the side of (place). Besides (with s) = plus, also.

data.meaning: in addition to, or also
data.tip: Beside = by the side of (place). Besides (with s) = plus, also.

data.meaning: in the space separating two (or a few clearly separate) things
data.example: The bank is between the café and the hotel.
data.tip: Between for separate, named things (between you and me). Among for a group or crowd (among the students).

data.meaning: in the middle of, or part of a group
data.tip: Between for separate, named things (between you and me). Among for a group or crowd (among the students).

data.meaning: feeling tired and unhappy because nothing interests you
data.tip: -ed describes how a person feels (bored). -ing describes the thing that causes the feeling (boring).

data.meaning: not interesting
data.tip: -ed describes how a person feels (bored). -ing describes the thing that causes the feeling (boring).

data.meaning: to take something that you will give back
data.tip: You borrow FROM someone; someone lends something TO you. Borrow = take, lend = give.

data.meaning: to give something that will be given back to you
data.example: Can you lend me your pen?
data.tip: You borrow FROM someone; someone lends something TO you. Borrow = take, lend = give.

data.meaning: to carry something toward the speaker or the place you're talking about
data.example: Bring your swimsuit when you come.
data.tip: Bring = toward here. Take = away from here to there.

data.meaning: to carry something away from the speaker to another place
data.example: Take an umbrella when you go out.
data.tip: Bring = toward here. Take = away from here to there.

data.meaning: to look at something to see if it is correct or safe
data.tip: Check = look and verify. Control = have power over. (Learners often say "control" when they mean "check", for example at an airport.)

data.meaning: to have power over something, or make it do what you want
data.tip: Check = look and verify. Control = have power over. (Learners often say "control" when they mean "check", for example at an airport.)

data.meaning: to move toward the speaker or the listener
data.tip: Come = toward me or you. Go = to another place. "I'm coming!" means "I'm moving toward you."

data.meaning: to move away from the speaker to another place
data.tip: Come = toward me or you. Go = to another place. "I'm coming!" means "I'm moving toward you."

data.meaning: something that goes well with something else
data.tip: A complement completes something (both have "comple"). A compliment is nice to hear (I like compliments).

data.meaning: something nice you say about someone
data.tip: A complement completes something (both have "comple"). A compliment is nice to hear (I like compliments).

data.meaning: to break or spoil a thing
data.tip: Damage things (a car, a house). Injure bodies (an arm, a person in an accident). Harm is general: health, people, the environment.

data.meaning: to hurt a person or animal, or have a bad effect
data.tip: Damage things (a car, a house). Injure bodies (an arm, a person in an accident). Harm is general: health, people, the environment.

data.meaning: to hurt a person's or animal's body, usually in an accident
data.example: She injured her knee playing soccer.
data.tip: Damage things (a car, a house). Injure bodies (an arm, a person in an accident). Harm is general: health, people, the environment.

data.meaning: at some time within a period, or through all of it
data.example: I fell asleep during the movie.
data.tip: For answers "how long?" (for two hours). During answers "when?" (during the meeting).

data.meaning: showing how long something lasts
data.example: I lived there for three years.
data.tip: For answers "how long?" (for two hours). During answers "when?" (during the meeting).

data.meaning: about the economy or money
data.example: The country is in an economic crisis.
data.tip: Economic is about the economy. Economical is about saving money: an economical car uses little fuel.

data.meaning: not using much money, fuel or time
data.tip: Economic is about the economy. Economical is about saving money: an economical car uses little fuel.

data.meaning: to leave your country to live in another
data.tip: Emigrate = Exit your country (emigrate from). Immigrate = come In (immigrate to).

data.meaning: to come into a new country to live
data.tip: Emigrate = Exit your country (emigrate from). Immigrate = come In (immigrate to).

data.meaning: to make certain that something happens
data.example: Please ensure the door is locked.
data.tip: Insure is about insurance (both start with "insur"). Ensure means make sure.

data.meaning: to buy insurance for something
data.tip: Insure is about insurance (both start with "insur"). Ensure means make sure.

data.meaning: above all, more than others
data.tip: Especially = particularly, most of all. Specially = for one special purpose (specially made, specially designed).

data.meaning: for a special purpose
data.example: This cake was specially made for you.
data.tip: Especially = particularly, most of all. Specially = for one special purpose (specially made, specially designed).

data.meaning: feeling happy and enthusiastic
data.example: The kids are excited about the trip.
data.tip: -ed is how you feel (excited). -ing is what makes you feel it (exciting).

data.meaning: causing excitement
data.tip: -ed is how you feel (excited). -ing is what makes you feel it (exciting).

data.meaning: at a greater physical distance
data.example: The hotel is farther than I thought.
data.tip: Farther is about physical distance (it has "far" in it). Further is for more of something: further information, further discussion.

data.meaning: more, additional, or to a greater degree
data.example: Do you have any further questions?
data.tip: Farther is about physical distance (it has "far" in it). Further is for more of something: further information, further discussion.

data.meaning: a smaller number of (countable nouns)
data.tip: Fewer for things you can count (fewer people). Less for things you can't count (less water, less time).

data.meaning: a smaller amount of (uncountable nouns)
data.tip: Fewer for things you can count (fewer people). Less for things you can't count (less water, less time).

data.meaning: enjoyable, or enjoyment
data.tip: Fun = you enjoy it. Funny = it makes you laugh (or it's strange).

data.meaning: making you laugh, or strange
data.tip: Fun = you enjoy it. Funny = it makes you laugh (or it's strange).

data.meaning: difficult, or with a lot of effort
data.tip: Hard (adverb) = with effort. Hardly = almost not. "He works hard" and "He hardly works" mean opposite things!

data.meaning: almost not
data.tip: Hard (adverb) = with effort. Hardly = almost not. "He works hard" and "He hardly works" mean opposite things!

data.meaning: to notice sounds with your ears
data.tip: You hear without trying; you listen on purpose. Listen needs "to" before an object.

data.meaning: to pay attention to sounds on purpose
data.tip: You hear without trying; you listen on purpose. Listen needs "to" before an object.

data.meaning: important in history
data.tip: Historic = famous or important (a historic day). Historical = connected with the past (a historical film).

data.meaning: about the past, or based on history
data.tip: Historic = famous or important (a historic day). Historical = connected with the past (a historical film).

data.meaning: to suggest something without saying it directly
data.tip: The speaker implies; the listener infers. Imply sends the message, infer receives it.

data.meaning: to reach a conclusion from information
data.example: What can we infer from the data?
data.tip: The speaker implies; the listener infers. Imply sends the message, infer receives it.

data.meaning: wanting to know more about something
data.tip: You are interested IN something; the thing is interesting.

data.meaning: holding your attention
data.tip: You are interested IN something; the thing is interesting.

data.meaning: belonging to it
data.tip: It's always means "it is" or "it has". Possessive its has no apostrophe, just like his and hers.

data.meaning: short for "it is" or "it has"
data.tip: It's always means "it is" or "it has". Possessive its has no apostrophe, just like his and hers.

data.meaning: the regular paid position you have
data.tip: Job is countable (a job, two jobs). Work as a noun is uncountable (a lot of work, not "a work").

data.meaning: activity you do to earn money or achieve something; the place you work
data.example: I have a lot of work today.
data.tip: Job is countable (a job, two jobs). Work as a noun is uncountable (a lot of work, not "a work").

data.meaning: final, or the one before now
data.example: This is the last bus tonight.
data.tip: Latest = newest (there may be more later). Last = final (no more after it), or the one before now.

data.meaning: the newest or most recent
data.example: Have you seen her latest movie?
data.tip: Latest = newest (there may be more later). Last = final (no more after it), or the one before now.

data.meaning: after the expected time
data.tip: Late = not on time. Lately = recently (often with the present perfect).

data.meaning: recently
data.tip: Late = not on time. Lately = recently (often with the present perfect).

data.meaning: to be in a flat position (no object); past: lay, lain
data.tip: Lay needs an object: you lay something down. Lie has no object: you lie down. The confusing part: the past of lie is lay.

data.meaning: to put something down flat (needs an object); past: laid
data.example: Lay the baby on the bed.
data.tip: Lay needs an object: you lay something down. Lie has no object: you lie down. The confusing part: the past of lie is lay.

data.meaning: to turn your eyes toward something on purpose
data.tip: See happens naturally. Look is short and on purpose (look at). Watch is longer, usually something that moves or changes.

data.meaning: to notice with your eyes
data.example: I can see the mountains from here.
data.tip: See happens naturally. Look is short and on purpose (look at). Watch is longer, usually something that moves or changes.

data.meaning: to look at something for a time, usually something moving
data.tip: See happens naturally. Look is short and on purpose (look at). Watch is longer, usually something that moves or changes.

data.meaning: to stop having something, or not win
data.tip: Lose has lost an o. Loose is "loooose", like a loose belt with extra room.

data.meaning: not tight or not firmly fixed
data.tip: Lose has lost an o. Loose is "loooose", like a loose belt with extra room.

data.meaning: to create or produce something
data.tip: Make is for creating something new (a cake, a plan, a mistake). Do is for tasks and activities (homework, the dishes, exercise).

data.meaning: to perform an action, task or job
data.example: I do my homework after dinner.
data.tip: Make is for creating something new (a cake, a plan, a mistake). Do is for tasks and activities (homework, the dishes, exercise).

data.meaning: belonging to or about one person
data.tip: Personal is about a person (stress on the first syllable). Personnel is staff (stress on the last syllable: per-son-NEL).

data.meaning: the people who work for an organization
data.tip: Personal is about a person (stress on the first syllable). Personnel is staff (stress on the last syllable: per-son-NEL).

data.meaning: the head of a school, or the most important
data.tip: The principal is your pal (the head of the school), and principal also means main. A principle is a rule (both end in -le).

data.meaning: a basic belief or rule
data.tip: The principal is your pal (the head of the school), and principal also means main. A principle is a rule (both end in -le).

data.meaning: making little or no noise
data.tip: Quiet ends in -et, like "silent" has a t. Quite ends in -te and changes how strong an adjective is.

data.meaning: fairly, or completely
data.tip: Quiet ends in -et, like "silent" has a t. Quite ends in -te and changes how strong an adjective is.

data.meaning: to keep something in your memory, or bring it back
data.tip: You remember something yourself. Someone else reminds you (remind needs a person after it).

data.meaning: to make someone remember something
data.tip: You remember something yourself. Someone else reminds you (remind needs a person after it).

data.meaning: to go up (no object)
data.example: The sun rises in the east.
data.tip: Raise needs an object: you raise something. Rise happens by itself: something rises.

data.meaning: to lift or increase something (needs an object)
data.tip: Raise needs an object: you raise something. Rise happens by itself: something rises.

data.meaning: to take money or things from a person or place illegally
data.tip: You rob a person or a place. You steal a thing. Thieves rob a bank and steal the money.

data.meaning: to take something that isn't yours
data.tip: You rob a person or a place. You steal a thing. Thieves rob a bank and steal the money.

data.meaning: to speak words
data.tip: You tell SOMEONE something, but you say something (TO someone). Tell usually needs a person after it.

data.meaning: to give information to someone
data.tip: You tell SOMEONE something, but you say something (TO someone). Tell usually needs a person after it.

data.meaning: practical and reasonable
data.tip: Sensible = good sense, practical. Sensitive = feels things strongly. (In many languages the word for sensitive looks like sensible.)

data.meaning: easily upset or affected; or understanding other people's feelings
data.example: She's very sensitive about her weight.
data.tip: Sensible = good sense, practical. Sensitive = feels things strongly. (In many languages the word for sensitive looks like sensible.)

data.meaning: from a point in time until now
data.tip: Since + a starting point (since Monday, since 2019). For + a length of time (for three days, for ten years).

data.meaning: showing a length of time
data.example: I've lived here for five years.
data.tip: Since + a starting point (since Monday, since 2019). For + a length of time (for three days, for ten years).

data.meaning: not moving
data.example: The car was stationary at the lights.
data.tip: Stationery with an e is envelopes and paper. Stationary with an a is standing still.

data.meaning: paper, pens and other things for writing
data.tip: Stationery with an e is envelopes and paper. Stationary with an a is standing still.

data.meaning: at that time, or next, after that
data.example: We had lunch and then went for a walk.
data.tip: Than is for compArison (both have an a). Then is for time (both have an e, like "when").

data.meaning: used to compare two things
data.example: She is taller than her brother.
data.tip: Than is for compArison (both have an a). Then is for time (both have an e, like "when").

data.meaning: in or at that place; also used to say something exists
data.tip: There has "here" inside it (a place). Their has "heir" (someone who owns things). They're = they are.

data.meaning: belonging to them
data.tip: There has "here" inside it (a place). Their has "heir" (someone who owns things). They're = they are.

data.meaning: short for "they are"
data.tip: There has "here" inside it (a place). Their has "heir" (someone who owns things). They're = they are.

data.meaning: toward a place, or before a verb
data.tip: Too has an extra o: it means "extra" or "also". Two is the number. To is everything else.

data.meaning: also, or more than needed
data.tip: Too has an extra o: it means "extra" or "also". Two is the number. To is everything else.

data.meaning: the number 2
data.tip: Too has an extra o: it means "extra" or "also". Two is the number. To is everything else.

data.meaning: going to other places in general
data.tip: Travel is the general activity (usually uncountable as a noun). A trip is a visit (there and back). A journey is the act of going from A to B.

data.meaning: going somewhere and coming back, usually for a short time
data.example: We took a trip to the mountains.
data.tip: Travel is the general activity (usually uncountable as a noun). A trip is a visit (there and back). A journey is the act of going from A to B.

data.meaning: traveling from one place to another, especially a long way
data.tip: Travel is the general activity (usually uncountable as a noun). A trip is a visit (there and back). A journey is the act of going from A to B.

data.meaning: if (used to talk about choices)
data.example: I don't know whether to go.
data.tip: Weather is about the sky (both have "ea" like "heat"). Whether is about a choice ("whether or not").

data.meaning: the conditions outside: rain, sun, wind
data.tip: Weather is about the sky (both have "ea" like "heat"). Whether is about a choice ("whether or not").

data.meaning: the person or people that (subject)
data.tip: If you can answer with he/she, use who. If you can answer with him/her, use whom (him and whom both end in m).

data.meaning: the person or people that (object, formal)
data.example: To whom should I send this?
data.tip: If you can answer with he/she, use who. If you can answer with him/her, use whom (him and whom both end in m).

data.meaning: belonging to which person
data.tip: If you can say "who is" or "who has", write who's. Otherwise it's whose.

data.meaning: short for "who is" or "who has"
data.tip: If you can say "who is" or "who has", write who's. Otherwise it's whose.

data.meaning: to get a prize or be first in a game or competition
data.tip: You earn money by working. You win a prize, a game or the lottery by luck or skill.

data.meaning: to get money for work
data.tip: You earn money by working. You win a prize, a game or the lottery by luck or skill.

data.meaning: belonging to you
data.tip: If you can say "you are" in the sentence, write you're. If not, write your.

data.meaning: short for "you are"
data.tip: If you can say "you are" in the sentence, write you're. If not, write your.
